headline: Profitability rebounds on narrower spandex losses
summary_short: Tayho's Q2 FY2026 EPS was ¥0.04, up 100% q/q from ¥0.02 and up 100% y/y from ¥0.02, as the spandex segment's losses narrowed sharply and aramid sales grew.
summary_long: EPS of ¥0.04 doubled both sequentially (from ¥0.02) and year-over-year (from ¥0.02). Tayho's H1 2026 earnings forecast — the only company disclosure locatable ahead of the full report — attributes the improvement to the spandex segment posting a much smaller loss on firmer industry supply-demand and lower unit costs, while the aramid segment grew sales via targeted marketing; meta-aramid profit fell on product-mix shifts, but para-aramid profit rose on production optimization and dynamic pricing. No revenue, margin, or balance-sheet figures are available from the shard or the located disclosure; the company gave no forward guidance.

drivers.explanation: Company attributes the improvement to a steep loss reduction in the spandex segment on better industry supply-demand and cost efficiencies, plus targeted-marketing-driven sales growth in the aramid segment.

Company's H1 2026 preliminary forecast states net profit will be positive and higher year-over-year, describing overall operating conditions as markedly improved with profitability partially restored versus the prior-year period.
